items.note: S2.1.3 states that three invocations exchange the banks up to sign, giving (x,y)->(-y,x), and restore every scratch wire. The sub-steps follow the proof at 741-765: the row roles of the schedule, the net change (JV+RG)x independent of a,c, the bit and complex coefficient cancellations, and the three stages. The setup values h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3, and the wire counts at 767-783, are not given.

The plan gives the invariant 'stored = D_v applied to logical' and the commutation of a common frame with a pointwise gate, so the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}. It also gives the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} for every role. This is exactly the argument at 804-825.

The result is stated correctly: triple lines are orthogonal for neighbours, source/sink sums are N and Wm-N, the only decrease is at center 3->4 (losing h), L=Ich, the budget is Wm-2N+2L, binary residuals have orthonormal bases, and the ratios are 100/539 and 101/539. The route matches the lemma's proof. However, the stage transitions and the gate-label table eq:motif-labels (899-990) are never given. Comparability is only asserted (S2.1.5.1.3), and so is the residual table (1021-1043) from which the dimensions are read, so an essential step is missing.

The plan assigns P_U to gates and sinks and -P_{U_a} to sources, so rank equals the dimension change, with the N exceptional edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one. It derives s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b with deficit N-2L_b>0 and the endpoint identity P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m, as in 1156-1171.

The plan states the per-edge content correctly: one translation kernel aI+bX_v (or its inverse) per orthonormal residual vector, s_c child calls in total, and s_c<W_cm. It does not define the phase frames C_U=H^{otimes m}diag(i^{q_U})H^{otimes m}, does not give s_c=W_cm-2N+2L_c, and does not state that after diagonal corrections every role receives C^{otimes m}. The weight-additivity proof (1231-1315) is not reconstructed.

The paper's chain is reproduced: L/N<1/2 gives the deficit N-2L>0 and s<Wm; both eta exceed 20*2^{-50} and log m<20, so m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-eta) and s_b/W_b<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}. The exact eta values (1322-1324) are omitted, and s_c/W_c<m^sigma appears only as a<=m^sigma in S2.2.3.7.

The plan states the O(V) elementary operations (digit permutations, digit moves, splitting, cyclic row split into W streams) and the controlled shift or unit scaling. The offset-preparation condition b^{O(1)} is carried by the quote. Both are infer steps with no derivation.

Both lemmas are stated and their proofs followed step by step. The factorization uses topmost-row, rightmost-pivot elimination. The shear choice of the odd prime q, the descending-order triangular updates, the E_1 Pi E_2 schedule and the one-interchange realization of H_i<-H_i+D_j give exactly a interchanges plus O(V).

The plan follows the proof of prop:power-interchange: m fields of b=e/m digits, cyclic row split into W role streams, Phi_{A_e} on edges via matrix-shear, the frame identity giving H<-H+D on every row, and the three-update interchange. It then gives s calls of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the two-case geometric sum giving O(e^tau), and the fixed-tape parking argument.

The plan follows the proof: high digits rho=O(log e) form a row field R=q^{2rho}>=W^k, zero rows pad it to R'<2R, the base-m pieces go to the power-width interchange at total O(Ve^tau), and binary ranges are padded to [q^e] for O(Vu^tau). The unequal-width variant (1740-1762) is only used, in S4.2.5 and S6.5.

The plan covers the C identities, the conjugation P_M X_v P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv} applied per column, and one forward child per kernel via (C^{-1})^{otimes f}=(-i)^f Z C Z. Binary row additions come from Gaussian elimination, and s_c child calls fall on f=e/m axes per slot. Finally H_0^{otimes D}=b^D S_D C^{otimes D} S_D, as in 1835-1940.

The plan follows the proof of the eight packed additions: the result (u+c(1-2(u mod 2)),w), one cyclic shift per line, the guard interval and bad set with delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}, and repair of B by sorting because T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes B. It then handles the top position by a two-bit XOR and gives the cost decomposition. The headline O(V(L^tau+1)) is the family simplification, with the full terms in S2.2.2.8.

The plan has s calls per node, node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), q_0 row chunks giving W^{k_0} rows, the u=Wg+w split with children of volume V/W, and F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e). It bounds internal and leaf costs with a<=m^sigma and sums over the base-m pieces to O(d^{lambda'}), matching 2286-2448.

The plan states the layer with one final truncation in O(Vd^{lambda'}) and error below sqrt2*2^{-p}. It derives the guard width through A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E (using s, not s/W), the bound 8B^2d^{nu+1}, the total 128mB^2d^{nu+3}<=C_0d^{C_1} with C_1=20, and Delta=o(p). It closes with the H_0 conversion and the disk truncation argument of 2736-2757.

The plan covers character cancellation without division, F_t^+F_t^-=I/t, the DIF step, bit-reversed storage B_tF_t^-, and the reverse procedure F_t^+B_t^{-1}. It then covers the layout L by prefix moves and chunk exchanges, one simultaneous layer per round, J_E Q_p=Q_p J_E, the error sqrt2*l*2^{-p} and the operators LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}. The round count in S3.2.3 is slightly loose (see errors).

The plan follows the proof: B_0=2^{4p}, four products by the established multiplier, the separation |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, two's-complement packing with carry in {-1,0}, centered extraction with carry in {0,1}, negacyclic reduction, and an O(rp log(rp)) cost.

The plan gives M_r=(f*g)/(rM), with error sqrt2*M(3l+1)2^{-p} and the stated cost. It derives F^-(f*g)=M F^-f F^-g, P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v), the error budget 3delta+eta scaled by M, and T/r products, as in 3414-3495.

The plan has P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, derived from the HvdH identity, a Neumann inversion of N=CTD and the rescalings S',J',D' with product 2^{-2alpha^2}. The selection C is an ordered scan, with errors below p^2 and the stated time. The permutations stay inside the identity. The tensor form, linewise padding, dp^2 error, line counts and O(d^2) axis moves follow 3836-3896.

The plan states and proves both identities: the chirp period and coefficient computation for QF_t u, and RF^+_s R=F^+_s from F_q^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F_q^+. A permutation commutes with pointwise products, and the normalizations give (u*v)/S^2. Conjugation yields RF_s^+.

The plan gives all fixed exponents and size parameters and the prime-interval estimate with eta=1/(4d). Distinct odd primes come from disjoint intervals, T/2<S<T by Bernoulli, and alpha^4 theta_i>p. Trial division takes n^{o(1)}, there is no wraparound since 2q-2<S, and c_j<2^{3b}, matching 4049-4193.

The plan shows Phi is an isomorphism because the image of x has order S. It gives the triangular formula b_i=a_i+mu_i sum_{j<i}a_jP_j and the update order d..1. Padded rotations fix [s_i,t_i), the updates are prefix-controlled shifts, and O(d^2) axis moves give O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)).

The plan covers the well-definedness of x_d->zeta y, the diagonal isomorphism, and the wrap identity zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j. M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T, and the twist errors below 4h_p are in S5.2.2 and S5.2.5.

The plan gives the source transform (A linewise, chirp transform, B_0 linewise, scale by 2^gamma), with exact counterpart RF_s and opposite version by conjugation. It lists the six-step algorithm with the two scales S and 2^{2b+4}S and explains their roles via (u*v)/S^2. The digit scaling 2^{-b-2} appears only through 'norm below 1/4'.

The plan follows the paper's error chain: E_ring=M(3L+2)<5TL, then 6TL, 8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, z with norm <.5 and error 2E_s+2, and E_w=S(3E_s+2)<28*2^gamma T^2L. The final bound 448b2^{-b+gamma}<=448b2^{-3b/4}<1/2 uses gamma<=b/4. Rounding, carries and the 2n-bit output complete the chain.

The plan covers V=Tp, the seven margins g_1..g_7 with min g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa, and the row-by-row justification of the table. Setup p^{A+C}=o(Tp) and exceptional sorting o(V) are bounded, log factors are absorbed by p^kappa, and schoolbook multiplication handles small n. S6.3's 'g_1,g_5,g_6>1/8' is weaker than the paper's g_1,g_6>1/2 but true.
No step mentions the Schonhage-Strassen conjecture, the eventual lower bound, or why an O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) machine refutes it. S0's motivation only says scanning at each level costs Theta(n log n).

errors.says: Each of the ell chunk rounds is one simultaneous layer, costing O(Tpd^{lambda'}) per round and O(Tp ell d^{lambda'}) in total.
errors.paper: The rounds on the remaining chunks are the qK rounds h=ell-2,...,b (3058-3063). The rest are a possible leading round and up to b+1<=K prefix rounds done by individual butterflies (3106-3128). Only the total is bounded by at most ell rounds (3103-3104, 4868), so there are not ell chunk rounds.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound. Two fixed networks with s<Wm give the address interchange O(Vu^tau) and the simultaneous layer O(Vd^{lambda'}); these feed the synthetic transforms and ring convolution, then Gaussian resampling with the chirp and permutation cancellation, then the six-step algorithm with its exactness proof and the cost table with min margin 2kappa. The chain thins at its foundation. The network parameters h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are never given, and the gate-label table behind 'every edge joins comparable labels' is only asserted, so L=Ich and the ratio 100/539 are quoted rather than derived. The complex phase interface (the frames C_U, s_c=W_cm-2N+2L_c, and C^{otimes m} on every role) is likewise taken as given rather than reconstructed.

steps.note: The fixed linear network on banks X,Y with neighbour wires defined by triple intersections is reconstructed, including the exchange (x,y)->(-y,x) and the restoration of every scratch wire for arbitrary initial values. N and m appear only as roles (data wires per bank, label dimension); h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are not given, which is a gap in the quantities.

A common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, so the array network implements D_out S D_in^{-1}, each edge costs only a frame change D_vD_u^{-1}, and the route operator is eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}.

Nested nondegenerate labels are built from triple indicator lines (orthogonal for neighbours) in a label space of dimension m. Every edge joins comparable labels, and only the central 3->4 edges decrease, each losing h. The tensor space F^{otimes3} and the explicit label table are not spelled out, but the defining conditions are present.
For U subset V, P_V-P_U has rank dim V-dim U, so an edge costs its dimension change. The N source edges 2P_{U_a} are the rank-one exceptions.
Sources sum to N and sinks to Wm-N, signed changes telescope to Wm-2N, and L=Ich adds 2L, giving Wm-2N+2L. Adding the N source ranks gives s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b.
L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 are both below 1/2, so the deficit N-2L_b>0 and s_b<W_bm. The ratios are stated, not computed from L=Ich.

The endpoint difference P_{U_a^perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m for X_a and 0->I for the other roles gives M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m on every role. Through the Phi_M frames, the bit network yields H<-H+D on every row, scratch rows included.
A=E_1 Pi E_2 with lower triangular E_i and a pieces of Pi. The shear costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V) of triangular controlled shifts, so a node makes s recursive calls in all.
Children have volume V/W, so F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1). eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20 give s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, and the two-case geometric sum gives F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: All nine steps of the central saving are reconstructed in their roles, from the frames, labels, rank-equals-dimension and budget through to the shear on every role, the rank-many recursive interchanges and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. The weak points are C1, where the network's size parameters (h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3, m=h^3) are missing, and C3/C6, where the label table and the computation of L=Ich and 100/539 are asserted rather than shown.
